class Solution:
    def isPossibleToSplit(self, nums: List[int]) -> bool:
        from collections import Counter
        
        # Count the frequency of each number in the array
        counts = Counter(nums)
        
        # If any number appears more than twice, we cannot split it into two arrays
        # where elements are distinct, because we only have two arrays (nums1 and nums2).
        # A number appearing 3 times would force at least one array to have duplicates
        # (e.g., if we try to put 3 instances into 2 spots, by Pigeonhole Principle,
        # at least one spot gets 2).
        for count in counts.values():
            if count > 2:
                return False
                
        # If all numbers appear at most twice, we can always validly split them.
        # We can put one instance of every number into nums1, and the second
        # instance (if available) into nums2.
        return True
